sequence_description: Replay the exact same SAML Assertion ID that includes <OneTimeUse/> twice; second submission must be rejected if OneTimeUse is enforced (SAML Core 2.5.1.5). Includes a control login first to ensure the source/flow works.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_replay_onetimeuse_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_replay_onetimeuse_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted replay of a OneTimeUse SAML assertion (same Assertion/@ID used twice).

sequence_description: I2 replay test: submit the same SAML Assertion ID with <OneTimeUse/> twice, with an explicit session revocation between attempts to ensure replay protection is assertion-bound (not just session-bound). Second submission must be rejected.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attack_onetimeuse_replay_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attack_onetimeuse_replay_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted replayed OneTimeUse SAML assertion (same Assertion ID) even after session revocation; OneTimeUse/replay protection not enforced.

sequence_description: I2 replay: reuse the exact same SAML Assertion/@ID twice (no <OneTimeUse/>), with an explicit session revocation between attempts to ensure replay protection is assertion-bound rather than session-bound.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_replay_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_replay_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted replayed SAML assertion ID after session revocation; assertion replay protection may be missing or session-bound only.

sequence_description: I2 freshness: confirm normal SAML login works, then submit an expired assertion while also omitting the <Conditions> element to probe whether expiry enforcement is bypassed when Conditions are missing.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_expired_nocond_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_expired_nocond_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted an expired SAML assertion when Conditions were omitted; freshness enforcement may be bypassable.

sequence_description: Test whether enabling MFA on a user is coherently enforced across authentication paths by comparing password login vs SAML login for the same principal. Expected: if password login triggers MFA challenge/denial, SAML login should not silently succeed without equivalent MFA enforcement.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_mfa_victim_saml_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_mfa_victim_saml_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Flow coherence broken: SAML login succeeded for an MFA-protected user while password login required additional steps/was denied, indicating step skipping via alternate path.

sequence_description: I3 flow coherence: attempt to replay a previously used RelayState/InResponseTo context by submitting a second SAMLResponse using the same RelayState, to see if authentik incorrectly accepts an out-of-order/duplicate callback within the same browser session.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_duplicate_cb_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_duplicate_cb_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Flow coherence failure: authentik accepted a second ACS POST reusing the same RelayState/context (duplicate/out-of-order callback accepted).

sequence_description: I3 flow coherence under config change: perform a successful SAML login, then remove the SAML source endpoint (cleanup_auth_method) and immediately attempt SAML login again. The second attempt must fail; acceptance would indicate stale flow state or cached acceptance despite config change.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_dana_after_disable_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_dana_after_disable_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Flow coherence/config coherence failure: SAML login succeeded even after the SAML source endpoint was removed/disabled (stale flow state or cached acceptance).

sequence_description: I3 flow coherence under mid-flight config change: start an SP-initiated SAML flow, then remove the SAML source endpoint before posting the SAMLResponse. The callback must not be accepted after the source is removed (no stale flow acceptance).
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_after_removal_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_after_removal_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Flow coherence broken: authentik accepted a SAML callback even though the SAML source was removed mid-flight (stale flow/config acceptance).

sequence_description: I3 flow-coherence attack: start an SP-initiated SAML flow, remove the SAML source (ACS endpoint), then re-enable a SAML source with the same slug and attempt to complete the original in-flight flow. Expected: the old flow context must not be accepted after source replacement (no stale flow/session binding across config changes).
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attack_oldflow_victim_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attack_oldflow_victim_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Flow coherence violation: authentik accepted completion of an in-flight SAML flow after the SAML source was removed and re-created (stale flow/session binding across config change).

sequence_description: I5 attack: Submit a SAML assertion missing the entire <Conditions> element (no time bounds, no audience restriction) and check whether authentik (as SP) still grants a session. Includes a control SAML login on the same source to ensure the flow/source is functional.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_nocond_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_nocond_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted SAML assertion without <Conditions>, enabling authorization not bounded by upstream intent (time/audience).
